items.issue: purge-devlocal destroys files in the same run under `--apply --empty-trash-days 0` (any value < 1), defeating the trash-first safety net. process_store's loop calls trash_file() first, which creates .trash/<today>/ containing the moved files; the later empty_old_trash(store, now, 0) then matches that same batch, because batch_ts is midnight local so (now - batch_ts)/DAY is already > 0, and shutil.rmtree()s it. The file is gone from both the store and the trash, with no recovery window. The run's own summary line is actively misleading: it prints `trash=1 trash-batches-emptied=1`, and `trash=1` reads as 'recoverable in .trash/'.
items.reason: PRE-EXISTING and OUT OF SCOPE for PRD 00006, deliberately not fixed here. It predates this PRD: the trash_file-then-empty_old_trash ordering in process_store's main loop was not touched by this work, and task 10's contract explicitly said 'Do NOT touch empty_old_trash's own comparison'. Task 10's one-line reorder fixed only the nothing-was-trashed case (the cadence stamp), which is all PRD 00006 needed; the with-content case remains broken. NOT escalated to a batch halt because nothing in this batch causes the loss, the default --empty-trash-days is 30 (safe), and it takes an explicit sub-1 flag value to reach; halting the batch would stop unrelated work without making anything safer. Confirmed by the decision gate with a live reproduction, not taken on the reviewer's word: a 400-day-old artifact in a temp store, run with `--apply --empty-trash-days 0`, ended up absent from the store AND absent from .trash/<today>/ while the tool reported trash=1. Suggested fix for a follow-up PRD: have empty_old_trash skip the current run's own batch name, so a retention pass can never delete what the same run just trashed. WORTH A FOLLOW-UP PRD - it breaks the skill's core trash-first guarantee.
items.resolution: PRD 00070-purge-trash-first-guarantee-v1 (empty_old_trash skips the current run's batch)
